message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-1/2","derivation":"The source construction B(r)=-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) is retained from the earlier source-only body. It satisfies the identity r^2/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) = (2+r)/2 - sqrt(1+r), so that with C=0 and u=0 the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r vanishes exactly. I add C(r,u)=-1/2, a constant, to cancel the leading-order ur cross-term in the full residual E = ur + r^2/4 + (2+r+2u)*delta + delta^2. With delta = r^2*B + u*r*C, the leading terms are r^2(1/4+2B) + ur(1+2C); setting C=-1/2 nullifies the ur coefficient while B handles the r^2 coefficient to all orders in r (exact at u=0). Both bodies are smooth on an open neighbourhood of the closed outer rectangle because 1+r >= 1/2 > 0 for |r|<=1/2, keeping the square root on a positive domain. No new derivation is introduced; the B body is the documented source formula and C is a constant first-order correction.","inspect":[{"file_id":"MATH_SOURCES/03_R3_EXACT_QUOTIENT.md","limit":4096,"offset":0}],"note":"B is the source-only pure-remainder canceller (exact at u=0, all r in support). C=-1/2 is a leading-order cross-term cancel for successor stages with u!=0; it does not give exact full-residual cancellation for u!=0. Current-stage data all has u=0, so C has no numerical effect here. The sqrt(1+r) domain is safe on |r|<=1/2. This is a local coefficient-field operator, not a PDE certificate, not a global NS claim, and not a regrading of the archived R4 finite-root scope."}
